Summary adjusted with Beige Book insights:
- Policy stance and outlook: The FOMC maintained the federal funds rate at 0–0.25% and continued QE (at least $80B Treasuries and $40B agency MBS per month), consistent with average inflation targeting that tolerates moderately above-2% inflation for a time to anchor expectations. Administered rates (IORB 0.15%, ON RRP 0.05%, ON repo 0.25%) and forward guidance aim to keep financial conditions accommodative while monitoring progress toward maximum employment and sustained 2% inflation.
- Beige Book cross-check: Regional conditions point to continued strengthening—reports indicate increases in hiring and wages and a rebound in tourism, including in the New York District. These trends corroborate the national narrative of improving activity and labor market momentum.
- Bank credit channel: The July SLOOS shows stronger loan demand and easing in lending standards across C&I and consumer categories, with some easing in CRE (notably multifamily). This supports transmission of accommodative policy to households and businesses.
- Risk balance: While some sectors have not fully recovered and the outlook remains dependent on the course of the virus, the combination of improved regional activity and easier credit availability tilts near-term momentum more constructive. Financial stability vulnerabilities remain a watchpoint but do not outweigh the broadly positive backdrop.

Net effect: Compared with a purely cautious read, the Beige Book’s stronger hiring/wage/tourism signals and the SLOOS easing warrant a modestly more positive assessment.
